question.text: This man was the first to sign the Declaration of Independence; according to legend, he wanted King George to be able to see it without his reading glasses on.
question.clue: This first governor of an independent Massachusetts was closely aligned with Samuel Adams, and neither of them were pardoned by Thomas Gage following the Boston Tea Party.

swap.leadin: This battle saw the death of Joseph Warren.
swap.text: Name this Revolutionary War battle fought near Boston, mostly on nearby Breed's Hill.
swap.answerHtml: Battle of Bunker Hill [accept Battle of Breed’s Hill before mentioned]
swap.clue: William Prescott constructed a defensive redoubt at this battle, which resulted in the dismissal of Thomas Gage.

question.text: This Chief of Artillery founded the Society of the Cincinnati to preserve the ideals of the American Revolution. A near-impregnable "Fort" named for this man is often conflated with the Bullion Depository, which holds American gold reserves.
question.clue: In that role, this general led such men as du Plessis, whose troops almost single handedly repulsed a British advance at the Battle of Monmouth.

swap.text: During the Revolutionary War, the Green Mountain Boys captured this fort on Lake Champlain. This fort's cannons were then transported to Boston to help siege the city.
swap.clue: This fort's location near Lake Champlain made it useful in monitoring trade routes between New York and Canada.

question.leadin: General Howe occupied Philadelphia after this battle and forced Washington's army to winter at Valley Forge.
question.text: Name this British victory and largest battle of the Revolutionary War. It took place along a namesake creek which is a branch of the Christina River.
question.clue: General von Knyphausen led the flanking attack that ended this battle, which was followed by a defeat for Anthony Wayne known as the Paoli Massacre.

swap.text: This founding father created the "Join, or Die" image. He also invented the bifocals and ascertained the electric nature of lightning by flying a kite in a storm.
swap.clue: In 1785, this man co-authored the first treaty of friendship between Prussia and America.

question.leadin: Georgia did not initially send delegates to this conference, though Lyman Hall came as a delegate from the Parish of St. John's.
question.text: Name this convention that served as the first national government of the United States. This body sent the Olive Branch Petition to King George III.
question.clue: A letter sent to a member of this body notes that "all men would be tyrants if they could" and urged this body to "Remember the Ladies."

swap.leadin: Name some stuff about documents that preceded the American Revolution.
swap.text: This act placed direct tax on just all kinds of documents. Its namesake Congress met in 1765 and achieved its repeal in 1766.
swap.clue: A Congress named for this act held in New York passed the "Declaration of Rights and Grievances" which in part called for the end of taxation without representation.

question.leadin: This man was the godson of Horace Walpole and would go on to replace Philip Schuyler as the general in charge of American troops in New York.
question.text: Identify this general who suffered a severe defeat at the Battle of Camden. With Benedict Arnold, he had earlier defeated John Burgoyne at the Battle of Saratoga.
question.clue: This man's aide John Armstrong authored a letter to Washington demanding unfunded pensions in the Newburgh Conspiracy.

swap.leadin: Following the revelation of this plot, its namesake was denied a chance to serve under Lafayette on a Canadian campaign.
swap.text: Identify this plot to replace the commander-in-chief of the Continental Army with Horatio Gates.
swap.clue: Another member of this group defeated Arthur St. Clair in a Pennsylvania gubernatorial election and John Cadwalader shot this group's namesake in the mouth in a duel.

question.text: In 1814 Thomas Macdonough defeated a British Fleet under Captain Downie in this battle foiling George Prevost's planned invasion of New York.
question.clue: Before this battle, which was part of the siege of , William Prescott fortified the wrong location leading to a confusion over its name.

swap.leadin: Name these following about a race described in Greek myth.
swap.text: 1. points) On May 29, 1780, Tarleton overtook a force under Abraham Buford he believed to include South Carolina Governor John Rutledge and quickly defeated them, cementing his merciless reputation with his ruthless post-battle conduct.

question.leadin: While serving as the Continental Congress's envoy to France, Silas Deane used a type of this substance containing glycerine and cobalt chloride.
question.text: Name this substance used by a group whose leader Benjamin Tallmadge used the alias "John Bolton." James Jay invented a type of this substance known as the "sympathetic stain."
question.answerHtml: invisible ink [accept security ink; accept sympathetic ink; prompt on ink]

swap.leadin: Answer the following about various proposals and compromises at the American Constitutional Convention.
swap.text: This Pennsylvania delegate nominated George Washington for President. Known as the "financier of the Revolution," this man became Superintendent of Finance in the early 1780's and later recommended Alexander Hamilton for the Secretary of Treasury position.
swap.clue: The panic of 1797 caused him to fall into debt, though the Bankruptcy Act of 1801 was written specifically to release him from prison.

question.text: During the American Revolution, the Americans responded to the Cherry Valley and Wyoming Massacres with this 1779 punitive expedition that burned the towns and crops of the Iroquois in the Finger Lakes region.

swap.text: During the Time of Troubles, Michael Romanov's Saltykov mother was forced to become a nun and adopt this name. A 15th-century "mayoress" with this name resisted Ivan III's siege of Novgorod.
swap.clue: While living on Cherry Street, a woman with this first name corresponded with Lucy Flucker Knox and hosted the son of the Marquis de Lafayette.

question.leadin: A conflict named for a specific one of these objects was sparked when a Wappinger woman was shot dead by a resident of New Amsterdam.
question.text: Identify these objects, which also name a 1734 riot in New Hampshire about particularly large ones requisitioned for British military use.
question.clue: A Parson Weems biography relates how a six year old boy destroyed one of these objects.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Benjamin Franklin's relations with Native Americans in the lead-up to American independence.
swap.text: After hearing of their massacre of 20 Susquehannock, Franklin led a delegation to disperse the Paxton Boys at this place. George Washington was able to retreat to Valley Forge despite losing at Brandywine and at this area near Philadelphia in October 1777.

question.text: Each year, Vermonters celebrate Bennington Battle Day, which honors this general's victory at the 1777 Battle of Bennington. He coined the phrase "live free or die," which is the motto of his home state, New Hampshire.
question.clue: This American general attacked Friedrich Baum, who had been sent by John Burgoyne, and overwhelmed him in the Battle of Bennington.

swap.text: The company which built the large canal of this name in New Jersey owned many of Indiana's canals after the bankruptcy. This is also the surname of a man who chaired the Erie Canal Commission and wrote the preamble to the U.S. Constitution.
swap.answerHtml: Morris [accept Morris Canal or Gouverneur Morris] (The common-link isn’t accidental, as Morris, New Jersey is named for Gouverneur Morris’s family.)
swap.clue: This was the surname of the so-called "Financier of the Revolution" from Pennsylvania and a New Yorker who wrote the Constitution's preamble.
